⏺ I've found the bugs. There are three in cloudflare_worker.js:                                        
                                                                                          
  1. Double-backslash unicode escapes in the GET FILE regex (lines 222, 223, 226) — [\\u00A0...] treats
   \, u, etc. as literal chars instead of unicode characters. The DELETE ONE handler at lines 202-204  
  uses the correct single-backslash form.                                                              
  2. Missing POST /media/box-XX/note handler — saving notes writes to R2 but there's no POST handler   
  for non-upload paths, so it falls through to unsupported_media_route 404.                            
  3. Missing /search-index GET/POST handlers — the route falls through to the KV redirect handler and  
  returns a 302/404 instead of JSON.

⏺ Three bugs fixed in cloudflare_worker.js:
                                                                                          
  1. Regex escape fix — [\\u00A0\\u202F\\u2007] → [\u00A0\u202F\u2007] on the three GET FILE           
  candidate-key lines. Without this, files with non-breaking or narrow spaces couldn't be served.      
  2. POST handler for note/meta — added POST /media/box-XX/<path> (for paths other than upload) to     
  write raw content to R2. This restores saving notes and file metadata.                               
  3. /search-index routes — added GET (reads _search-index.json from R2) and POST (writes it) handlers.
   Without these, search index rebuild/load/save were silently failing via the KV redirect fallback.

⏺ Pushed. Here's what was wrong and what's fixed:

  The root cause: loadCover was reading from the R2 _cover file, but editBoxSave was only writing the
  cover to the KV search-index — never to R2. So after a page reload, the _cover file didn't exist in
  R2 and the cover was lost.

  Three fixes applied:
  1. editBoxSave now POSTs the cover filename to /media/box-XX/_cover in R2 after every save
  2. openEditBoxModal reads the current cover from R2 _cover first (not search-index), so the picker
  shows the right selection
  3. Worker LIST filters out _cover so it won't appear as a regular file

  You need to redeploy the Cloudflare Worker (copy cloudflare_worker.js into the Workers dashboard) for
   the LIST filter change. The index.html fix is already live via GitHub Pages.

⏺ The issue is that loadCover now makes a _cover fetch for every one of the 50 boxes on page load.
  That's 50+ extra requests which can hit the rate limit (120/min), causing loadSearchIndex to fail
  silently and searchIndex to stay empty — no file search results.

  The fix: revert loadCover to read from searchIndex first (already in memory, zero extra requests).
  The _cover R2 file is only needed by the edit modal picker — which we already handle.

⏺ Pushed. The problem was that the previous loadCover change was making a _cover fetch for every one of
   the 50 boxes on page load — 50+ requests hitting the 120 req/min rate limit, which caused the
  loadSearchIndex call to get throttled, leaving searchIndex empty and breaking file search.

  The fix: loadCover now reads coverFile directly from the already-loaded in-memory searchIndex (no
  network request), so covers still persist correctly and search is unaffected. The _cover R2 file is
  still written on save and read when opening the edit modal.

⏺ Pushed. Here's what was wrong and what's fixed:

  The root cause: loadCover was reading from the R2 _cover file, but editBoxSave was only writing the
  cover to the KV search-index — never to R2. So after a page reload, the _cover file didn't exist in
  R2 and the cover was lost.

  Three fixes applied:
  1. editBoxSave now POSTs the cover filename to /media/box-XX/_cover in R2 after every save
  2. openEditBoxModal reads the current cover from R2 _cover first (not search-index), so the picker
  shows the right selection
  3. Worker LIST filters out _cover so it won't appear as a regular file

  You need to redeploy the Cloudflare Worker (copy cloudflare_worker.js into the Workers dashboard) for
   the LIST filter change. The index.html fix is already live via GitHub Pages.

⏺ Pushed. The problem was that the previous loadCover change was making a _cover fetch for every one of
   the 50 boxes on page load — 50+ requests hitting the 120 req/min rate limit, which caused the
  loadSearchIndex call to get throttled, leaving searchIndex empty and breaking file search.

  The fix: loadCover now reads coverFile directly from the already-loaded in-memory searchIndex (no
  network request), so covers still persist correctly and search is unaffected. The _cover R2 file is
  still written on save and read when opening the edit modal.

⏺ Pushed. Here's what was wrong and why it kept failing:

  Root cause: box.js had no version string in the <script> tag. Your browser was caching the old
  version (which never called updateSearchIndex after uploads at all), so every fix I made to box.js
  was invisible to you.

  What's fixed now:
  - The script tag is now box.js?v=5 — your browser will load the fresh version on next visit
  - After uploading, you'll see "Upload complete · search index updated ✓" in the status bar confirming
   the index was actually saved

  What to do: Go to any box page, wait for it to load (you'll get the new box.js automatically), then
  upload a file. When you see "search index updated ✓", go to the home page and search — it should find
   it. For files already in box-04 and box-05, use ↺ Rebuild search index on the home page.

⏺ Pushed. Here's what was wrong and what's fixed:

  The root cause: loadCover was reading from the R2 _cover file, but editBoxSave was only writing the
  cover to the KV search-index — never to R2. So after a page reload, the _cover file didn't exist in
  R2 and the cover was lost.

  Three fixes applied:
  1. editBoxSave now POSTs the cover filename to /media/box-XX/_cover in R2 after every save
  2. openEditBoxModal reads the current cover from R2 _cover first (not search-index), so the picker
  shows the right selection
  3. Worker LIST filters out _cover so it won't appear as a regular file

  You need to redeploy the Cloudflare Worker (copy cloudflare_worker.js into the Workers dashboard) for
   the LIST filter change. The index.html fix is already live via GitHub Pages.

  Root cause: box.js had no version string in the <script> tag. Your browser was caching the old
  version (which never called updateSearchIndex after uploads at all), so every fix I made to box.js
  was invisible to you.

  What's fixed now:
  - The script tag is now box.js?v=5 — your browser will load the fresh version on next visit
  - After uploading, you'll see "Upload complete · search index updated ✓" in the status bar confirming
   the index was actually saved

  What to do: Go to any box page, wait for it to load (you'll get the new box.js automatically), then
  upload a file. When you see "search index updated ✓", go to the home page and search — it should find
   it. For files already in box-04 and box-05, use ↺ Rebuild search index on the home page.

⏺ Pushed. Here's what was wrong and what's fixed:

  The root cause: loadCover was reading from the R2 _cover file, but editBoxSave was only writing the
  cover to the KV search-index — never to R2. So after a page reload, the _cover file didn't exist in
  R2 and the cover was lost.

  Three fixes applied:
  1. editBoxSave now POSTs the cover filename to /media/box-XX/_cover in R2 after every save
  2. openEditBoxModal reads the current cover from R2 _cover first (not search-index), so the picker
  shows the right selection
  3. Worker LIST filters out _cover so it won't appear as a regular file

  You need to redeploy the Cloudflare Worker (copy cloudflare_worker.js into the Workers dashboard) for
   the LIST filter change. The index.html fix is already live via GitHub Pages.

  Root cause: box.js had no version string in the <script> tag. Your browser was caching the old
  version (which never called updateSearchIndex after uploads at all), so every fix I made to box.js
  was invisible to you.

  What's fixed now:
  - The script tag is now box.js?v=5 — your browser will load the fresh version on next visit
  - After uploading, you'll see "Upload complete · search index updated ✓" in the status bar confirming
   the index was actually saved

  What to do: Go to any box page, wait for it to load (you'll get the new box.js automatically), then
  upload a file. When you see "search index updated ✓", go to the home page and search — it should find
   it. For files already in box-04 and box-05, use ↺ Rebuild search index on the home page.

⏺ Pushed. Here's what was wrong and what's fixed:

  The root cause: loadCover was reading from the R2 _cover file, but editBoxSave was only writing the
  cover to the KV search-index — never to R2. So after a page reload, the _cover file didn't exist in
  R2 and the cover was lost.

  Three fixes applied:
  1. editBoxSave now POSTs the cover filename to /media/box-XX/_cover in R2 after every save
  2. openEditBoxModal reads the current cover from R2 _cover first (not search-index), so the picker
  shows the right selection
  3. Worker LIST filters out _cover so it won't appear as a regular file

  You need to redeploy the Cloudflare Worker (copy cloudflare_worker.js into the Workers dashboard) for
   the LIST filter change. The index.html fix is already live via GitHub Pages.

   the 50 boxes on page load — 50+ requests hitting the 120 req/min rate limit, which caused the
  loadSearchIndex call to get throttled, leaving searchIndex empty and breaking file search.

  The fix: loadCover now reads coverFile directly from the already-loaded in-memory searchIndex (no
  network request), so covers still persist correctly and search is unaffected. The _cover R2 file is
  still written on save and read when opening the edit modal.

  Root cause: box.js had no version string in the <script> tag. Your browser was caching the old
  version (which never called updateSearchIndex after uploads at all), so every fix I made to box.js
  was invisible to you.

  What's fixed now:
  - The script tag is now box.js?v=5 — your browser will load the fresh version on next visit
  - After uploading, you'll see "Upload complete · search index updated ✓" in the status bar confirming
   the index was actually saved

  What to do: Go to any box page, wait for it to load (you'll get the new box.js automatically), then
  upload a file. When you see "search index updated ✓", go to the home page and search — it should find
   it. For files already in box-04 and box-05, use ↺ Rebuild search index on the home page.

⏺ Pushed. Here's what changed:

  Description: Now stored as boxDesc — completely separate from boxNote (the box's notes). Editing the
  description on the home page no longer touches the notes in the box page, and vice versa. The card
  shows your boxDesc if set, otherwise falls back to the note content.

  Tags: Now stored as boxTags in the search index. They persist across page reloads, show on home page
  cards, and are searchable. Previously they were only in memory and wiped on reload.

  After the page deploys, you'll need to re-save any boxes where you previously set a description or
  tags (since the old values were stored in the wrong fields). Just open the edit modal and hit Save.

⏺ Pushed. Here's what was wrong and what's fixed:

  The root cause: loadCover was reading from the R2 _cover file, but editBoxSave was only writing the
  cover to the KV search-index — never to R2. So after a page reload, the _cover file didn't exist in
  R2 and the cover was lost.

  Three fixes applied:
  1. editBoxSave now POSTs the cover filename to /media/box-XX/_cover in R2 after every save
  2. openEditBoxModal reads the current cover from R2 _cover first (not search-index), so the picker
  shows the right selection
  3. Worker LIST filters out _cover so it won't appear as a regular file

  You need to redeploy the Cloudflare Worker (copy cloudflare_worker.js into the Workers dashboard) for
   the LIST filter change. The index.html fix is already live via GitHub Pages.

⏺ The issue is that loadCover now makes a _cover fetch for every one of the 50 boxes on page load.
  That's 50+ extra requests which can hit the rate limit (120/min), causing loadSearchIndex to fail
  silently and searchIndex to stay empty — no file search results.

  The fix: revert loadCover to read from searchIndex first (already in memory, zero extra requests).
  The _cover R2 file is only needed by the edit modal picker — which we already handle.

⏺ Pushed. The problem was that the previous loadCover change was making a _cover fetch for every one of
   the 50 boxes on page load — 50+ requests hitting the 120 req/min rate limit, which caused the
  loadSearchIndex call to get throttled, leaving searchIndex empty and breaking file search.

  The fix: loadCover now reads coverFile directly from the already-loaded in-memory searchIndex (no
  network request), so covers still persist correctly and search is unaffected. The _cover R2 file is
  still written on save and read when opening the edit modal.

  However, you do still need to redeploy the Cloudflare Worker (copy cloudflare_worker.js into the
  Workers dashboard) for one minor change: filtering _cover out of the file list so it doesn't appear
  as a regular file inside a box. It won't break anything if you skip it, but the _cover file will show
   up in the box's file list.

  Root cause: box.js had no version string in the <script> tag. Your browser was caching the old
  version (which never called updateSearchIndex after uploads at all), so every fix I made to box.js
  was invisible to you.

  What's fixed now:
  - The script tag is now box.js?v=5 — your browser will load the fresh version on next visit
  - After uploading, you'll see "Upload complete · search index updated ✓" in the status bar confirming
   the index was actually saved

  What to do: Go to any box page, wait for it to load (you'll get the new box.js automatically), then
  upload a file. When you see "search index updated ✓", go to the home page and search — it should find
   it. For files already in box-04 and box-05, use ↺ Rebuild search index on the home page.

  description on the home page no longer touches the notes in the box page, and vice versa. The card
  shows your boxDesc if set, otherwise falls back to the note content.

  cards, and are searchable. Previously they were only in memory and wiped on reload.

   (since the old values were stored in the wrong fields). Just open the edit modal and hit Save.

⏺ Pushed. Here's what was wrong and what's fixed:

  The root cause: loadCover was reading from the R2 _cover file, but editBoxSave was only writing the
  cover to the KV search-index — never to R2. So after a page reload, the _cover file didn't exist in
  R2 and the cover was lost.

  Three fixes applied:
  1. editBoxSave now POSTs the cover filename to /media/box-XX/_cover in R2 after every save
  2. openEditBoxModal reads the current cover from R2 _cover first (not search-index), so the picker
  shows the right selection
  3. Worker LIST filters out _cover so it won't appear as a regular file

  You need to redeploy the Cloudflare Worker (copy cloudflare_worker.js into the Workers dashboard) for
   the LIST filter change. The index.html fix is already live via GitHub Pages.

⏺ Pushed. Here's what changed:

  Description: Now stored as boxDesc — completely separate from boxNote (the box's notes). Editing the
  description on the home page no longer touches the notes in the box page, and vice versa. The card shows
  your boxDesc if set, otherwise falls back to the note content.

  Tags: Now stored as boxTags in the search index. They persist across page reloads, show on home page
  cards, and are searchable. Previously they were only in memory and wiped on reload.

  After the page deploys, you'll need to re-save any boxes where you previously set a description or tags
  (since the old values were stored in the wrong fields). Just open the edit modal and hit Save.

⏺ Pushed. Here's what was wrong and what's fixed:

  The root cause: loadCover was reading from the R2 _cover file, but editBoxSave was only writing the
  cover to the KV search-index — never to R2. So after a page reload, the _cover file didn't exist in
  R2 and the cover was lost.

  Three fixes applied:
  1. editBoxSave now POSTs the cover filename to /media/box-XX/_cover in R2 after every save
  2. openEditBoxModal reads the current cover from R2 _cover first (not search-index), so the picker
  shows the right selection
  3. Worker LIST filters out _cover so it won't appear as a regular file

  You need to redeploy the Cloudflare Worker (copy cloudflare_worker.js into the Workers dashboard) for
   the LIST filter change. The index.html fix is already live via GitHub Pages.

  That's 50+ extra requests which can hit the rate limit (120/min), causing loadSearchIndex to fail
  silently and searchIndex to stay empty — no file search results.

  The fix: revert loadCover to read from searchIndex first (already in memory, zero extra requests).
  The _cover R2 file is only needed by the edit modal picker — which we already handle.

   the 50 boxes on page load — 50+ requests hitting the 120 req/min rate limit, which caused the
  loadSearchIndex call to get throttled, leaving searchIndex empty and breaking file search.

  The fix: loadCover now reads coverFile directly from the already-loaded in-memory searchIndex (no
  network request), so covers still persist correctly and search is unaffected. The _cover R2 file is
  still written on save and read when opening the edit modal.

   the index was actually saved

  upload a file. When you see "search index updated ✓", go to the home page and search — it should find
   it. For files already in box-04 and box-05, use ↺ Rebuild search index on the home page.

  (since the old values were stored in the wrong fields). Just open the edit modal and hit Save.

⏺ Pushed. Here's what was wrong and what's fixed:

  The root cause: loadCover was reading from the R2 _cover file, but editBoxSave was only writing the
  cover to the KV search-index — never to R2. So after a page reload, the _cover file didn't exist in
  R2 and the cover was lost.

  Three fixes applied:
  1. editBoxSave now POSTs the cover filename to /media/box-XX/_cover in R2 after every save
  2. openEditBoxModal reads the current cover from R2 _cover first (not search-index), so the picker
  shows the right selection
  3. Worker LIST filters out _cover so it won't appear as a regular file

  You need to redeploy the Cloudflare Worker (copy cloudflare_worker.js into the Workers dashboard) for
   the LIST filter change. The index.html fix is already live via GitHub Pages.

⏺ Pushed. The problem was that the previous loadCover change was making a _cover fetch for every one of
   the 50 boxes on page load — 50+ requests hitting the 120 req/min rate limit, which caused the
  loadSearchIndex call to get throttled, leaving searchIndex empty and breaking file search.

  The fix: loadCover now reads coverFile directly from the already-loaded in-memory searchIndex (no
  network request), so covers still persist correctly and search is unaffected. The _cover R2 file is
  still written on save and read when opening the edit modal.

⏺ Pushed. Here's what was wrong and why it kept failing:

  Root cause: box.js had no version string in the <script> tag. Your browser was caching the old
  version (which never called updateSearchIndex after uploads at all), so every fix I made to box.js
  was invisible to you.

  What's fixed now:
  - The script tag is now box.js?v=5 — your browser will load the fresh version on next visit
  - After uploading, you'll see "Upload complete · search index updated ✓" in the status bar confirming
   the index was actually saved

  What to do: Go to any box page, wait for it to load (you'll get the new box.js automatically), then
  upload a file. When you see "search index updated ✓", go to the home page and search — it should find
   it. For files already in box-04 and box-05, use ↺ Rebuild search index on the home page.

  your boxDesc if set, otherwise falls back to the note content.

  (since the old values were stored in the wrong fields). Just open the edit modal and hit Save.

⏺ Pushed. Here's what was wrong and what's fixed:

  The root cause: loadCover was reading from the R2 _cover file, but editBoxSave was only writing the
  cover to the KV search-index — never to R2. So after a page reload, the _cover file didn't exist in
  R2 and the cover was lost.

  Three fixes applied:
  1. editBoxSave now POSTs the cover filename to /media/box-XX/_cover in R2 after every save
  2. openEditBoxModal reads the current cover from R2 _cover first (not search-index), so the picker
  shows the right selection
  3. Worker LIST filters out _cover so it won't appear as a regular file

  You need to redeploy the Cloudflare Worker (copy cloudflare_worker.js into the Workers dashboard) for
   the LIST filter change. The index.html fix is already live via GitHub Pages.

  Root cause: box.js had no version string in the <script> tag. Your browser was caching the old
  version (which never called updateSearchIndex after uploads at all), so every fix I made to box.js
  was invisible to you.

  What's fixed now:
  - The script tag is now box.js?v=5 — your browser will load the fresh version on next visit
  - After uploading, you'll see "Upload complete · search index updated ✓" in the status bar confirming
   the index was actually saved

  What to do: Go to any box page, wait for it to load (you'll get the new box.js automatically), then
  upload a file. When you see "search index updated ✓", go to the home page and search — it should find
   it. For files already in box-04 and box-05, use ↺ Rebuild search index on the home page.

  Description: Now stored as boxDesc — completely separate from boxNote (the box's notes). Editing the
  description on the home page no longer touches the notes in the box page, and vice versa. The card shows
  your boxDesc if set, otherwise falls back to the note content.

  Tags: Now stored as boxTags in the search index. They persist across page reloads, show on home page cards,
  and are searchable. Previously they were only in memory and wiped on reload.

  After the page deploys, you'll need to re-save any boxes where you previously set a description or tags
  (since the old values were stored in the wrong fields). Just open the edit modal and hit Save.

⏺ Pushed. Here's what was wrong and what's fixed:

  The root cause: loadCover was reading from the R2 _cover file, but editBoxSave was only writing the
  cover to the KV search-index — never to R2. So after a page reload, the _cover file didn't exist in
  R2 and the cover was lost.

  Three fixes applied:
  1. editBoxSave now POSTs the cover filename to /media/box-XX/_cover in R2 after every save
  2. openEditBoxModal reads the current cover from R2 _cover first (not search-index), so the picker
  shows the right selection
  3. Worker LIST filters out _cover so it won't appear as a regular file

  You need to redeploy the Cloudflare Worker (copy cloudflare_worker.js into the Workers dashboard) for
   the LIST filter change. The index.html fix is already live via GitHub Pages.

  still written on save and read when opening the edit modal.

⏺ Pushed. Here's what was wrong and why it kept failing:

  Root cause: box.js had no version string in the <script> tag. Your browser was caching the old
  version (which never called updateSearchIndex after uploads at all), so every fix I made to box.js
  was invisible to you.

  What's fixed now:
  - The script tag is now box.js?v=5 — your browser will load the fresh version on next visit
  - After uploading, you'll see "Upload complete · search index updated ✓" in the status bar confirming
   the index was actually saved

  What to do: Go to any box page, wait for it to load (you'll get the new box.js automatically), then
  upload a file. When you see "search index updated ✓", go to the home page and search — it should find
   it. For files already in box-04 and box-05, use ↺ Rebuild search index on the home page.

⏺ Pushed. Here's what changed:

  Description: Now stored as boxDesc — completely separate from boxNote (the box's notes). Editing the
  description on the home page no longer touches the notes in the box page, and vice versa. The card shows
  your boxDesc if set, otherwise falls back to the note content.

  Tags: Now stored as boxTags in the search index. They persist across page reloads, show on home page cards,
  and are searchable. Previously they were only in memory and wiped on reload.

  After the page deploys, you'll need to re-save any boxes where you previously set a description or tags
  (since the old values were stored in the wrong fields). Just open the edit modal and hit Save.

  coverFile from the existing entry. Any boxDesc/boxTags fields get dropped. The fix is to use Object.assign —
   start from the existing entry and only override the fields box.js actually owns (boxNote, files). That way 
  ALL other fields are automatically preserved, forever.

⏺ Pushed. The root fix is one line in box.js:                                                                 
                                                                                          
  Before (fragile — manually lists fields to preserve):                                                       
  var entry = {boxId, boxNote, files};                                                                        
  if(existing) entry.coverFile = ...; entry.boxDesc = ...; entry.boxTags = ...;                               
                                                                                                              
  After (robust — preserves everything):                                                                      
  var entry = Object.assign({}, existing || {}, {boxId, boxNote, files});                                     
                                                                         
  This means box.js now starts from whatever is already in the search index entry and only overrides the three
   fields it owns. boxDesc, boxTags, coverFile, and anything added in future will never be touched by the box 
  page again.
                                                                                                              
  The no-cache meta tag and ?v=6 ensure your browser won't run a stale version of box.js going forward.

⏺ Pushed. Here's what was wrong and what's fixed:

  The root cause: loadCover was reading from the R2 _cover file, but editBoxSave was only writing the
  cover to the KV search-index — never to R2. So after a page reload, the _cover file didn't exist in
  R2 and the cover was lost.

  Three fixes applied:
  1. editBoxSave now POSTs the cover filename to /media/box-XX/_cover in R2 after every save
  2. openEditBoxModal reads the current cover from R2 _cover first (not search-index), so the picker
  shows the right selection
  3. Worker LIST filters out _cover so it won't appear as a regular file

  You need to redeploy the Cloudflare Worker (copy cloudflare_worker.js into the Workers dashboard) for
   the LIST filter change. The index.html fix is already live via GitHub Pages.

⏺ The issue is that loadCover now makes a _cover fetch for every one of the 50 boxes on page load.
  That's 50+ extra requests which can hit the rate limit (120/min), causing loadSearchIndex to fail
  silently and searchIndex to stay empty — no file search results.

  The fix: revert loadCover to read from searchIndex first (already in memory, zero extra requests).
  The _cover R2 file is only needed by the edit modal picker — which we already handle.

⏺ Pushed. The problem was that the previous loadCover change was making a _cover fetch for every one of
   the 50 boxes on page load — 50+ requests hitting the 120 req/min rate limit, which caused the
  loadSearchIndex call to get throttled, leaving searchIndex empty and breaking file search.

  The fix: loadCover now reads coverFile directly from the already-loaded in-memory searchIndex (no
  network request), so covers still persist correctly and search is unaffected. The _cover R2 file is
  still written on save and read when opening the edit modal.

  Workers dashboard) for one minor change: filtering _cover out of the file list so it doesn't appear
  as a regular file inside a box. It won't break anything if you skip it, but the _cover file will show
   up in the box's file list.

  - After uploading, you'll see "Upload complete · search index updated ✓" in the status bar confirming
   the index was actually saved

  What to do: Go to any box page, wait for it to load (you'll get the new box.js automatically), then
  upload a file. When you see "search index updated ✓", go to the home page and search — it should find
   it. For files already in box-04 and box-05, use ↺ Rebuild search index on the home page.

  coverFile from the existing entry. Any boxDesc/boxTags fields get dropped. The fix is to use Object.assign —
  start from the existing entry and only override the fields box.js actually owns (boxNote, files). That way
  ALL other fields are automatically preserved, forever.

⏺ Pushed. The root fix is one line in box.js:

  Before (fragile — manually lists fields to preserve):
  var entry = {boxId, boxNote, files};
  if(existing) entry.coverFile = ...; entry.boxDesc = ...; entry.boxTags = ...;

  After (robust — preserves everything):
  var entry = Object.assign({}, existing || {}, {boxId, boxNote, files});

  This means box.js now starts from whatever is already in the search index entry and only overrides the three
  fields it owns. boxDesc, boxTags, coverFile, and anything added in future will never be touched by the box
  page again.

  The no-cache meta tag and ?v=6 ensure your browser won't run a stale version of box.js going forward.

⏺ Pushed. Here's what was wrong and what's fixed:

  The root cause: loadCover was reading from the R2 _cover file, but editBoxSave was only writing the
  cover to the KV search-index — never to R2. So after a page reload, the _cover file didn't exist in
  R2 and the cover was lost.

  Three fixes applied:
  1. editBoxSave now POSTs the cover filename to /media/box-XX/_cover in R2 after every save
  2. openEditBoxModal reads the current cover from R2 _cover first (not search-index), so the picker
  shows the right selection
  3. Worker LIST filters out _cover so it won't appear as a regular file

  You need to redeploy the Cloudflare Worker (copy cloudflare_worker.js into the Workers dashboard) for
   the LIST filter change. The index.html fix is already live via GitHub Pages.

  - After uploading, you'll see "Upload complete · search index updated ✓" in the status bar confirming
   the index was actually saved

  What to do: Go to any box page, wait for it to load (you'll get the new box.js automatically), then
  upload a file. When you see "search index updated ✓", go to the home page and search — it should find
   it. For files already in box-04 and box-05, use ↺ Rebuild search index on the home page.

⏺ Pushed. Here's what changed:

  Description: Now stored as boxDesc — completely separate from boxNote (the box's notes). Editing the
  description on the home page no longer touches the notes in the box page, and vice versa. The card shows your
   boxDesc if set, otherwise falls back to the note content.

  Tags: Now stored as boxTags in the search index. They persist across page reloads, show on home page cards,
  and are searchable. Previously they were only in memory and wiped on reload.

  After the page deploys, you'll need to re-save any boxes where you previously set a description or tags
  (since the old values were stored in the wrong fields). Just open the edit modal and hit Save.

⏺ The real problem: in box.js, when updateSearchIndex runs, it builds a new entry object and only copies
  coverFile from the existing entry. Any boxDesc/boxTags fields get dropped. The fix is to use Object.assign —
  start from the existing entry and only override the fields box.js actually owns (boxNote, files). That way
  ALL other fields are automatically preserved, forever.

  ⎿  [main 413d2d2] Fix boxDesc overwrite: use Object.assign merge so box.js preserves all index fields

⏺ Pushed. The root fix is one line in box.js:

  Before (fragile — manually lists fields to preserve):
  var entry = {boxId, boxNote, files};
  if(existing) entry.coverFile = ...; entry.boxDesc = ...; entry.boxTags = ...;

  After (robust — preserves everything):
  var entry = Object.assign({}, existing || {}, {boxId, boxNote, files});

  This means box.js now starts from whatever is already in the search index entry and only overrides the three
  fields it owns. boxDesc, boxTags, coverFile, and anything added in future will never be touched by the box page
   again.

  The no-cache meta tag and ?v=6 ensure your browser won't run a stale version of box.js going forward.

⏺ Pushed. Three things fixed:                                                                                    
                                                                                          
  1. Tags now show — the tags div is always created on every card, so tags render immediately when you save them 
  and persist across reloads via the search index.                                                               
  2. Added boxes persist — box-51 (and any future additions) are saved to a _config entry in KV. On page load,   
  those boxes are re-added to the grid automatically. No more boxes.json editing needed.                         
  3. Deleted boxes persist — deleted boxes stay gone after refresh, also via _config.                            
                                                                                                                 
  The "Remember to update boxes.json" alert is gone. The 50 boxes in boxes.json are the base list; additions and 
  deletions on top of that are stored in KV.

⏺ The box/ folder only has index.html — there's no duplicate. What you saw in the GitHub sidebar was the full    
  repo tree with all root files listed together, which made it look like duplicates. The structure is:
                                                                                                                 
  boxes/                                                                                                         
  ├── box/              
  │   └── index.html      ← the per-box page                                                                     
  ├── box.js              ← script loaded by box/index.html                                                      
  ├── boxes.json          ← base box list                                                                        
  ├── cloudflare_worker.js                                                                                       
  └── index.html          ← home page                                                                            
                                                                                                                 
  box.js and boxes.json live in the root and are referenced from box/index.html via ../box.js and ../boxes.json. 
  No redundancy.

⏺ Box number: You'd enter 11 again — or any number you want. The system doesn't auto-increment; you choose the   
  number each time.                                                                                              
                                                                                                                 
  Data inheritance: If you deleted box-11 and re-add box-11, it will inherit the old data — files, notes, and    
  cover — because deletion only removes the card from the home page (the _config.deletedIds list), it doesn't    
  delete anything from R2 storage. The files are still there.                                                    
                                                            
  If you want a clean fresh box with no inherited data, use a new number (12, 13, etc.) instead of reusing 11.

⏺ Pushed. Here's how it works now:                                                                               
                                                                                          
  - Delete box → goes to recycle bin (files kept in R2, box hidden from home page)                               
  - 🗑 Trash (N) button appears in the admin bar whenever there are deleted boxes                                 
  - Restore → box reappears with its description, tags, cover, and all files intact                              
  - Delete permanently → wipes all R2 files and removes everything — truly gone                                  
                                                                                                                 
  So to answer your original question: if you delete box-11 and re-add it, you now get to choose — restore it    
  (inherits all data) or permanently delete it first (clean slate), then add a fresh box-11.

⏺ Pushed. The problem was that the previous loadCover change was making a _cover fetch for every one of
   the 50 boxes on page load — 50+ requests hitting the 120 req/min rate limit, which caused the
  loadSearchIndex call to get throttled, leaving searchIndex empty and breaking file search.

  The fix: loadCover now reads coverFile directly from the already-loaded in-memory searchIndex (no
  network request), so covers still persist correctly and search is unaffected. The _cover R2 file is
  still written on save and read when opening the edit modal.

❯ is it fixed? anything I should do?                                                                   

⏺ The code is deployed to GitHub Pages — no action needed on your end for the search fix.

  However, you do still need to redeploy the Cloudflare Worker (copy cloudflare_worker.js into the
  Workers dashboard) for one minor change: filtering _cover out of the file list so it doesn't appear
  as a regular file inside a box. It won't break anything if you skip it, but the _cover file will show
   up in the box's file list.

  box-04, you'll need to either upload a new file to that box (which triggers a reindex) or hit ↺
  Rebuild search index from the home page admin toolbar to index the existing files.

  upload a file. When you see "search index updated ✓", go to the home page and search — it should find
   it. For files already in box-04 and box-05, use ↺ Rebuild search index on the home page.

⏺ The real problem: in box.js, when updateSearchIndex runs, it builds a new entry object and only copies
  coverFile from the existing entry. Any boxDesc/boxTags fields get dropped. The fix is to use Object.assign —
  start from the existing entry and only override the fields box.js actually owns (boxNote, files). That way
  ALL other fields are automatically preserved, forever.

⏺ Pushed. The root fix is one line in box.js:

  Before (fragile — manually lists fields to preserve):
  var entry = {boxId, boxNote, files};
  if(existing) entry.coverFile = ...; entry.boxDesc = ...; entry.boxTags = ...;

  After (robust — preserves everything):
  var entry = Object.assign({}, existing || {}, {boxId, boxNote, files});

  This means box.js now starts from whatever is already in the search index entry and only overrides the three
  fields it owns. boxDesc, boxTags, coverFile, and anything added in future will never be touched by the box page
   again.

  The no-cache meta tag and ?v=6 ensure your browser won't run a stale version of box.js going forward.

⏺ Pushed. Three things fixed:

  1. Tags now show — the tags div is always created on every card, so tags render immediately when you save them
  and persist across reloads via the search index.
  2. Added boxes persist — box-51 (and any future additions) are saved to a _config entry in KV. On page load,
  those boxes are re-added to the grid automatically. No more boxes.json editing needed.
  3. Deleted boxes persist — deleted boxes stay gone after refresh, also via _config.

  The "Remember to update boxes.json" alert is gone. The 50 boxes in boxes.json are the base list; additions and
  deletions on top of that are stored in KV.

❯ the repo root directory has box.js and boxes.json and under boxes/box/ it sill have another set of box.js and  
  boxes.json. is this right? or redudant?                                                                        

  Listed 1 directory (ctrl+o to expand)

⏺ The box/ folder only has index.html — there's no duplicate. What you saw in the GitHub sidebar was the full
  repo tree with all root files listed together, which made it look like duplicates. The structure is:

  boxes/
  ├── box/
  │   └── index.html      ← the per-box page
  ├── box.js              ← script loaded by box/index.html
  ├── boxes.json          ← base box list
  ├── cloudflare_worker.js
  └── index.html          ← home page

  box.js and boxes.json live in the root and are referenced from box/index.html via ../box.js and ../boxes.json.
  No redundancy.

❯ say if I add the box 11, and then delete box 11. next day if add another box, what box number should I enter,  
  is it box 11 or box 12. And does the newly added box inherit the data in the orginal box 11?                   

⏺ Box number: You'd enter 11 again — or any number you want. The system doesn't auto-increment; you choose the
  number each time.

  Data inheritance: If you deleted box-11 and re-add box-11, it will inherit the old data — files, notes, and
  cover — because deletion only removes the card from the home page (the _config.deletedIds list), it doesn't
  delete anything from R2 storage. The files are still there.

  If you want a clean fresh box with no inherited data, use a new number (12, 13, etc.) instead of reusing 11.

⏺ Pushed. Here's how it works now:

  - Delete box → goes to recycle bin (files kept in R2, box hidden from home page)
  - 🗑 Trash (N) button appears in the admin bar whenever there are deleted boxes
  - Restore → box reappears with its description, tags, cover, and all files intact
  - Delete permanently → wipes all R2 files and removes everything — truly gone

  So to answer your original question: if you delete box-11 and re-add it, you now get to choose — restore it
  (inherits all data) or permanently delete it first (clean slate), then add a fresh box-11.

❯ now let's add the ability to change file names of each file uploaded,an option added to the ...menu. also in   
  each box page, let's add a Unique Identifier (UID) - editable. may be another toggle section with a few URL    
  text field. help me decide should we do a map preview for the URLs.                                            

⏺ Good questions. Let me give you my take before implementing:

  Rename file — straightforward, but needs a new worker endpoint since R2 has no native rename (it has to copy
  then delete server-side). Requires a worker redeploy.

  UID — simple editable field, stored in the search index. No issues.

  URL fields — I'd suggest a dynamic list of labelled links (e.g. "Purchase link", "Manual", "Location") rather
  than fixed fields. More flexible.

  Map preview — I'd recommend no. Reasons:
  - Google Maps embed requires a paid API key
  - Adds loading complexity and external dependency
  - A location URL already opens perfectly in Google Maps / Apple Maps when clicked
  - If you want a quick visual, a thumbnail screenshot service would need another API key

  Instead, I'd detect if a URL looks like a maps link and show a 📍 icon with "Open in Maps" — clean and zero
  cost.

  ---
  Before I start: can you clarify the URL section a bit?
  1. What kinds of URLs are you thinking — product pages, location, documents, or a general-purpose "any link"?
  2. How many URLs per box typically — 1–2 or could be many?

  That'll help me decide whether to do a fixed set of fields or a dynamic add/remove list.

  - Rename: new POST /media/box-XX/rename?from=old&to=new worker endpoint (server-side copy+delete, efficient for

  - UID: single editable text field in a collapsible "Box Info" section, saved to search index.
  - Links: dynamic list in the same section — each row is a label + URL, up to as many as needed, with
  add/remove. Saved to search index. URLs open in new tab; maps links get a 📍 icon.

  All three grouped in one collapsible panel on the box page to keep it clean.

⏺ Everything is wired up correctly. Here's a summary of what was done:                                           
                                                                                                                 
  3 features implemented:                                                                                        
                                                                                                                 
  1. Rename file — "Rename" added to the ⋯ context menu. Opens a modal pre-filled with the current filename;     
  press Enter or click Rename to commit. The worker does a server-side R2 copy+delete, then META keys are        
  updated. Requires worker redeploy (see below).                                                                 
  2. UID field — Editable text field in a collapsible "Box Info" card (same chevron-toggle pattern as Notes).    
  Stored as boxUid in the search index.                                                                          
  3. URL links — Dynamic list in the same "Box Info" card. Each row has a label input, URL input, an ↗
  open-in-new-tab button, and a ✕ remove button. Stored as boxLinks in the search index. Click "Save" to persist.
                                                            
  To go live: you need to redeploy cloudflare_worker.js since the rename endpoint is new. Everything else        
  (HTML/JS) is static and takes effect on next page load.

❯ do I do pbcopy < cloudflare_worker.js  and paste them in cloudflare dashboard area?                            
                                                                                                                 
⏺ Yes, that works. The steps:                                                                                    
                                                                                                                 
  1. pbcopy < cloudflare_worker.js — copies the file to your clipboard                                           
  2. Go to https://dash.cloudflare.com → Workers & Pages → click your worker (box-redirect)
  3. Click Edit Code                                                                                             
  4. Select all the existing code (⌘A) and paste (⌘V)                                                            
  5. Click Deploy                                                                                                
                                                                                                                 
  Alternatively, if you have Wrangler installed you can just run wrangler deploy from the project directory,     
  which is faster. But the copy-paste method works fine.

  pbcopy < cloudflare_worker.js                                                                                  
   
  Then paste in the dashboard editor.

❯ is it very risky to add another big function. a hierarchical folder sturcture in the list view. where files    
  can be organized like google drive. files can be selected and moved other folder. being able to add a new      
  folder within the box or a folder in the box.                                                                  
                                                                                                                 
⏺ Honest assessment: high risk, high complexity — it's the biggest architectural change you could make to this   
  app. Here's why:                       
                                                                                                                 
  What it touches:      
  - Worker needs new endpoints: list by prefix, create folder placeholder, move file (copy+delete across paths)  
  - Every existing file URL breaks if you restructure the key scheme (box-01/file.jpg → box-01/photos/file.jpg)  
  - The search index stores flat file arrays — needs rethinking for paths                                        
  - Upload, delete, rename, bulk-delete all need folder context awareness                                        
  - The entire file list UI needs a navigation state (current path, breadcrumbs, back button)                    
                                                                                                                 
  The honest tradeoff:                                                                                           
  Your boxes already have two organization tools — tags (on individual files) and captions. A typical box has    
  maybe 10–30 files. Folders inside a box would add a lot of UI complexity for a problem that tags mostly already
   solve.                                                   
                                                                                                                 
  If you still want it, the pragmatic path is:              
  - Flat "virtual folders" using filename prefixes (photos/pic.jpg) — no real folder objects, just path grouping
  - No moving existing files — folders only for new uploads                                                      
  - Single level deep (no subfolders) to keep it manageable
                                                                                                                 
  But I'd recommend against it for now. The tag + search system you have is genuinely sufficient for the scale   
  this app is designed for. If you're finding you need folders, it might mean a box has grown too large and      
  should be split into multiple boxes instead.                                                                   
                                                                                                                 
  Want me to help with something else, or do you still want to proceed with folders?

❯   - Flat "virtual folders" using filename prefixes (photos/pic.jpg) — no real folder objects, just path        
  grouping                                                                                                       
    - No moving existing files — folders only for new uploads                                                    
                                                                                                                 
    - Single level deep (no subfolders) to keep it manageable"   I need more info to understand what these mean. 
    "virtual folder", do I have to change file names to put files into virtual folders? I can stick wit single   
  level deep for now.                                                                                            
                                                                                                                 
⏺ Good questions. Let me explain clearly.                                                                        
                                         
  How R2 storage actually works:                                                                                 
  R2 has no real folders — everything is just a flat list of files with names (called "keys"). A "virtual folder"
   is just a naming trick: instead of storing sunset.jpg, you store photos/sunset.jpg. The slash in the name     
  looks like a folder to the UI, but it's really just part of the filename.                                      
                                                                                                                 
  Do you have to rename files to put them in folders?                                                            
  Not the visible filename — sunset.jpg still displays as sunset.jpg. But under the hood the storage key changes 
  from:                                                                                                          
  box-01/sunset.jpg          ← root (no folder)             
  box-01/photos/sunset.jpg   ← inside "photos" folder                                                            
                                                                                                                 
  What the experience would look like:
  - When you upload, you pick which folder to upload into (or stay in root)                                      
  - The UI shows folders as entries you can click into, then shows the files inside
  - Moving a file to a different folder = copy to new key + delete old key (like rename)                         
                                                                                                                 
  The constraint "no moving existing files" means:                                                               
  Your current files (box-01/sunset.jpg) stay where they are — shown in root. You wouldn't be able to drag them  
  into folders without a move operation. I can actually include move if we do this — I was being conservative    
  earlier.                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                 
  The constraint "single level deep" means:                                                                      
  box-01/
    ├── photos/       ← allowed                                                                                  
    │   └── pic.jpg                                         
    └── docs/         ← allowed
        └── file.pdf           
                    
  box-01/photos/vacation/  ← NOT allowed (two levels)                                                            
                                                     
  So: no, you don't rename files yourself. The folder is just a prefix the app manages for you. Does this make   
  sense for how you want to use it?                                                                              
   
❯ let me clarify. So visually, I still see folders in each box if I create the folder. and I am able to drag and 
   drop files into folders or use select files and click move button in an action bar.                           
                                                                                                                 
⏺ Yes, that's exactly achievable. Here's the full picture of what that means to build:                           
                                                                                                                 
  What you'd see:                                                                                                
  box-01/                      
    📁 photos        ← click to enter                                                                            
    📁 documents     ← click to enter                                                                            
    🖼 receipt.jpg   ← file in root                                                                               
                                                                                                                 
  Interactions:                                                                                                  
  - Click a folder → navigates inside, breadcrumb updates (Box-01 › photos)
  - Drag a file onto a folder → moves it in                                                                      
  - Select files → "Move" appears in action bar → folder picker modal
  - Upload button → uploads into whichever folder you're currently in                                            
  - "New folder" button → creates a folder                           
                                                                                                                 
  What needs to change:                                                                                          
                                                                                                                 
  ┌────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐                        
  │      Area      │                              Changes                               │
  ├────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Worker         │ New move endpoint (copy+delete with new path prefix)               │
  ├────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Worker         │ list endpoint needs to return folder entries at current depth      │                        
  ├────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ box.js         │ Current path state, navigation, folder rendering, drag-onto-folder │                        
  ├────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤                        
  │ box.js         │ Move modal, new folder button, breadcrumb                          │
  ├────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤                        
  │ box/index.html │ Folder row styles, breadcrumb styles, move modal HTML              │
  └────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘                        
                                                            
  One important question before I start: existing files (already uploaded with no folder) stay in the root —     
  they're fully movable into folders via drag or the action bar. That works fine.
                                                                                                                 
  This is a solid 300–400 lines of new code across 3 files plus a worker redeploy. It's the biggest single       
  feature so far. Want to go ahead?
                                                                                                                 
❯ let me clarify one more thing before we go ahead. the new folder created, can I remove the folder - and        
  everything under that folder gets removed as well. is this achievable?                                         
                                                                                                                 
⏺ Yes, fully achievable. Deleting a folder just means deleting all R2 files whose key starts with that prefix —  
  the worker already does something similar with "Delete ALL files in box." Folder delete would be a scoped      
  version of that.                                                                                               
   
  The behaviour would be:                                                                                        
  - Click ⋯ on a folder → Delete folder                     
  - Confirm prompt: "Delete 'photos' and all X files inside?"                                                    
  - All files under box-01/photos/ get wiped from R2         
  - Folder disappears from the list                                                                              
                                                                                                                 
  No extra complexity — it's a straightforward extension of what already exists.                                 
                                                                                                                 
  Ready to build the whole thing?
